scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic update has a valid authenticated manifest, but the resolver stages a different component identity than the component digest and immutable identity bound by that manifest.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock manifest verifier and in-memory staging slot record only synthetic component identities and read-only digests; no firmware code is executed or persistently flashed.
scenarios.positive_control: The same authenticated manifest resolves the intended immutable synthetic component and the in-memory staging receipt matches its authenticated digest and component identity.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep signer, manifest, device, hardware target, version, and rollback state constant while resolving a neighboring synthetic component with a distinct immutable identity.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, risks unrecoverable flash state, needs real signing keys, or would target an unauthorized device.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding resolver output to the authenticated component identity and digest, the substituted component is rejected while the intended component still stages successfully.
scenarios.device_policy_update_generation: Record synthetic device identity, hardware revision, normal update path, update attempt generation, current policy generation, and clean in-memory staging generation.
scenarios.manifest_signer_hardware_version: Bind fake signer/root, signer policy generation, canonical manifest identity, authenticated component fields, canonical hardware target, current version, target version, and rollback domain.
scenarios.component_set_transformed_artifact: Record one-component set identity, expected immutable component digest, actual resolver output identity, no transform ambiguity, and final synthetic bytes offered to staging.
scenarios.staging_activation_transaction: Capture staging target, staging generation, resolver-to-stage receipt, activation transaction identity, and prove the mismatch exists before any committed activation occurs.
scenarios.rollback_version_state_commit: Keep rollback/version state unchanged in this case and record the authoritative generation so version-state changes cannot explain the component substitution.
scenarios.recovery_fallback_policy: Run on the normal synthetic update path with recovery/fallback disabled; separately record that no alternate path or stale recovery policy participates in the decision.
scenarios.final_update_state_consumer: Identify the mock staging/update controller that accepts or rejects the resolved component and emits a read-only receipt naming manifest and staged identities.
scenarios.effective_update_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to staging one wrong inert synthetic component under an otherwise valid manifest identity in an owner-controlled fixture.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one in-memory staged-component marker and deterministic digest receipt; no boot selection, execution, persistent flash, or external device state changes.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate device, attempt generation, signer policy, canonical manifest, intended component, resolved component, staging generation, consumer decision, and receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold all update fields constant while changing only resolver output from authenticated immutable component identity to a different synthetic component identity.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject canonical alias equivalence, stale staging receipt, previous update attempt, manifest normalization equivalence, recovery fallback, or a different slot as causes.
scenarios.evidence_level: FWU3 because a mock read-only final update-state consumer accepts the wrong synthetic component identity into staging under the authenticated manifest context.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: FWU3 maximum until a bounded reversible activation/update-state effect plus complete transaction, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation evidence supports FWU4 or FWU5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A signed synthetic delta is accepted and applied using base generation N even though its authenticated update metadata requires current base generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled deterministic delta function reconstructs only inert synthetic bytes in memory, and a mock staging consumer reports a read-only output digest without flashing or execution.
scenarios.positive_control: Applying the authenticated synthetic delta to the required current base generation N+1 reconstructs the expected inert component digest and stages it once.
scenarios.negative_control: The same delta and manifest are paired with an unrelated base identity that fails both base-generation and expected reconstructed-digest controls before staging.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, risks unrecoverable flash state, needs real signing keys, or would target an unauthorized device.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding the delta to the authenticated base identity/generation and reconstructed output digest, stale base N is rejected while current N+1 remains accepted.
scenarios.device_policy_update_generation: Record device/revision, update path, attempt generation, policy generation, current installed component generation, and deterministic in-memory staging generation.
scenarios.manifest_signer_hardware_version: Bind fake signer, canonical manifest, target hardware, target version, rollback domain, authenticated delta identity, required base identity, and required base generation.
scenarios.component_set_transformed_artifact: Record signed delta identity, actual base identity/generation, deterministic transform identity, reconstructed component identity, expected digest, and actual output digest.
scenarios.staging_activation_transaction: Capture whether reconstructed output reaches staging, its staging generation, activation transaction identity, and ensure no committed activation is needed for the oracle.
scenarios.rollback_version_state_commit: Pin rollback/version state across controls and record it read-only so stale base acceptance cannot be confused with a permitted downgrade or rollback exception.
scenarios.recovery_fallback_policy: Use only the normal synthetic update path and record that recovery, fallback, alternate slot, and manufacturing policies are inactive for this fixture.
scenarios.final_update_state_consumer: Identify the mock staging controller that consumes the reconstructed component and emits an inert receipt containing base generation and output digest.
scenarios.effective_update_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to accepting one reconstructed inert component derived from the wrong synthetic delta-base generation in a controlled fixture.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an in-memory reconstructed-component marker and digest receipt; no real firmware image, executable payload, or persistent device state is produced.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind device attempt, manifest, delta identity, required and actual base generations, transform identity, reconstructed digest, staging consumer, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold delta, signer, manifest, hardware, target version, transform, and consumer constant while changing only base generation N versus required N+1.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject intentionally content-equivalent bases, transform nondeterminism, stale output cache, manifest aliasing, independent parser defect, or another update-attempt receipt.
scenarios.evidence_level: FWU3 because an inert staging consumer accepts a reconstructed synthetic component produced from the wrong authenticated delta-base generation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: FWU3 maximum until a bounded reversible activation or committed update-state effect and full delta/base/remediation provenance justify higher promotion.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic update commits rollback/version state before durable component-set activation, so a controlled interruption leaves the authoritative counter advanced while activation remains uncommitted.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A fake rollback counter, in-memory component slots, and mock activation controller record only reversible journal state and read-only transaction receipts under controlled interruption.
scenarios.positive_control: The corrected transaction commits the synthetic component-set activation before or atomically with the authoritative rollback/version-state transition and recovers to one known state.
scenarios.negative_control: An interruption before either activation or counter commit leaves both synthetic activation and rollback state unchanged, proving the harness can represent a clean aborted transaction.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, risks unrecoverable flash state, needs real signing keys, or would target an unauthorized device.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After transactional ordering or atomic journaling is repaired, interruption at each modeled boundary recovers to either old/old or new/new component and rollback generations.
scenarios.device_policy_update_generation: Record device/revision, update attempt generation, signer policy generation, current installed component generation, staging generation, and activation transaction generation.
scenarios.manifest_signer_hardware_version: Use a valid fake signer, canonical manifest, correct hardware target, current-to-new target version, and one rollback domain so commit ordering is the only changed dimension.
scenarios.component_set_transformed_artifact: Use a fully authenticated inert component set with deterministic digests and no delta or extraction ambiguity, keeping artifact identity constant across interruption controls.
scenarios.staging_activation_transaction: Trace complete staging, activation authorization, activation request, durable activation commit, transaction journal generation, interruption point, and recovered activation state.
scenarios.rollback_version_state_commit: Record fake authoritative rollback counter before write, pending write, durable commit identity/generation, activation commit ordering, and post-recovery authoritative counter.
scenarios.recovery_fallback_policy: Use a deterministic transaction-recovery routine with a fixed current recovery policy; no alternate signer or downgrade exception is allowed during journal recovery.
scenarios.final_update_state_consumer: Identify the mock update transaction controller that reports final activated component-set identity and authoritative rollback generation after simulated restart/recovery.
scenarios.effective_update_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to creating an inconsistent reversible synthetic update state where rollback/version authority and activated component generations disagree.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a fake transaction journal showing advanced rollback generation with old activation state, entirely in memory and resettable between runs.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind attempt generation, staged set, activation transaction, interruption point, activation commit, rollback-state commit, recovery generation, final consumer, and receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold bundle, signer, hardware, version, component set, and recovery logic fixed while changing only activation-versus-rollback commit ordering around the same interruption.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject advisory counter semantics, staging-only status, previous-attempt journal residue, safe documented asymmetric recovery, duplicate retry, or wrong transaction receipt.
scenarios.evidence_level: FWU4 because a bounded reversible synthetic transaction reaches an inconsistent committed update-state effect tied to activation and rollback-counter ordering.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: FWU4 maximum until complete interruption-state provenance, meaningful counterfactuals, alternative elimination, receipt binding, and remediation replay satisfy FWU5.

scenarios.hypothesis: Recovery-mode update acceptance uses stale recovery policy generation N even though the authoritative current recovery signer/version/hardware policy has advanced to generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A synthetic recovery path with fake signers and an inert mock activation controller emits only read-only policy and acceptance receipts; no real recovery image is flashed or executed.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic recovery bundle under current policy generation N+1 uses the authorized fake signer, valid hardware target, permitted version, and expected inert acceptance receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A synthetic signer that is invalid under both N and N+1 is rejected before staging, proving the recovery verifier is active and the stale-policy distinction is observable.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, risks unrecoverable flash state, needs real signing keys, or would target an unauthorized device.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After recovery policy lookup is bound to the current generation, stale N signer/version authority is rejected while the explicitly allowed N+1 recovery update remains accepted.
scenarios.device_policy_update_generation: Record device/revision, recovery path identity, update attempt generation, normal policy generation, stale recovery policy N, current recovery policy N+1, and staging generation.
scenarios.manifest_signer_hardware_version: Bind canonical recovery manifest, fake signer identity, recovery signer authorization, canonical hardware target, current/target version, and rollback domain under N and N+1.
scenarios.component_set_transformed_artifact: Use one immutable inert recovery component with identical bytes and digest across controls so only policy generation changes, with no transform or delta ambiguity.
scenarios.staging_activation_transaction: Capture recovery staging generation, activation transaction identity, and whether the same inert component is admitted under stale versus current policy before any boot semantics.
scenarios.rollback_version_state_commit: Record the recovery path's documented rollback/version rule and authoritative state without mutating it, proving stale policy rather than counter drift drives acceptance.
scenarios.recovery_fallback_policy: Bind recovery/fallback path identity, stale and current recovery policy generations, authorized signer sets, version exceptions, hardware scope, and transition-back policy.
scenarios.final_update_state_consumer: Identify the inert recovery update controller that accepts/rejects the component and emits a read-only receipt naming path, policy generation, signer, and staging state.
scenarios.effective_update_trust_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to accepting one inert synthetic recovery update under a stale recovery policy generation in an owner-controlled fixture.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one in-memory recovery staging marker and policy receipt, with no flash persistence, boot execution, production key use, or external device effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate device, recovery path, update attempt, stale/current policy generation, signer, manifest, component identity, staging consumer, and deterministic receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold recovery bundle, component, hardware target, target version, staging consumer, and path constant while changing only recovery policy generation N versus N+1.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject documented recovery exception, normal-path policy assumptions, previous-attempt receipt, alias signer identity, hardware alias equivalence, or another recovery transaction.
scenarios.evidence_level: FWU3 because a mock read-only recovery update consumer accepts an inert component under the wrong recovery policy generation without requiring boot execution.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: FWU3 maximum until a bounded reversible committed recovery-update effect and complete policy/transaction/remediation provenance justify FWU4 or FWU5.
